cd /Users/makky/Downloads/AI-Research-Lab-main/research/2026-11-12-llm-based-vs-traditional-static-analysis/papers/guo2025repoaudit && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='analysis.md'
s=open(p).read()
old="- [I] Contradicts later independent evaluation: li2026llm re-ran RepoAudit on overlapping targets (linux/mm, linux/sound, linux/drivers/net, linux/drivers/peci, ImageMagick) and found 0 detections on known CWE-401/416 cases and 92.77% SFDR. Based on li2026llm Tables IV and VII."
new="""- [I] Documented tension with the later independent evaluation in li2026llm. Both sides are confirmed in the texts, but li is not a replication on the same bugs. Based on the pages cited below.
  - Effectiveness. guo: all 21 previously reported bugs are reproduced and 19 new ones found, for 40 TPs / 11 FPs and a precision of 78.43% on 15 C/C++ projects (p. 7, Table 2 p. 8). li: RepoAudit (Sonnet 3.5) detects 0 of 110 and RepoAudit (GPT-5.4) 2 of 110 known C/C++ vulnerabilities [@li2026llm, p. 7]. Its real-world SFDR is 92.77%, a 9-project average [@li2026llm, p. 11].
  - Dataset. guo's "Old" bugs are bug reports from prior tools/papers (p. 7; Table 2 caption, p. 8). li's 0/110 comes from its *controlled* ReposVul set. That set uses "the three repositories with the most cases" per CWE, and li does not name them [@li2026llm, p. 5]. The shared targets are linux/sound, linux/mm, linux/drivers/net, linux/drivers/peci and ImageMagick (Table 1, p. 7; [@li2026llm, p. 6]). They appear only in li's *real-world* set, where recall is not measured. For 3 of the 5 the bug type differs:
    - ImageMagick: NPD here, CWE-401 in li.
    - linux/driver/net: MLK here, CWE-416 in li.
    - peci: UAF here, CWE-476 in li.

    Module sizes also differ: net is 914,025 LoC here vs 3,924,621 LOC in li. On these projects li's RepoAudit (Sonnet 3.5) emits 0 warnings (linux/sound, linux/mm, ImageMagick), 1 warning (linux/drivers/net, an FP) and 3 warnings (peci, all FPs) [@li2026llm, p. 11].
  - Commit. guo analyses the versions used by the earlier works. Its new bugs are found "in historic versions", 14 of them fixed in the latest commit (p. 7, p. 8). li uses current commits: 6093a68 for Linux and 3bf1076 for ImageMagick [@li2026llm, p. 6]. guo's 4 Linux known bugs are all intra-procedural (Table 2, p. 8), as li also notes [@li2026llm, p. 7].
  - Metric. guo reports precision on the tool's own reports plus reproduction of 21 known bugs (p. 17). li reports recall on CVEs and SFDR [@li2026llm, p. 6].
  - Labeller. guo does not describe how RepoAudit's reports were judged; only the Infer/CodeGuru reports are said to be checked manually (p. 14). li labels warnings with Codex and validates manually [@li2026llm, p. 11].
  - Explanation (ours). Target selection, code version, bug-type mapping, scale, metric and labeller all differ, so the results are not directly comparable. li records 0.00 input tokens for RepoAudit on at least one project [@li2026llm, p. 16] and attributes all 108/108 misses of RepoAudit (GPT-5.4) to incomplete API modelling / candidate exploration [@li2026llm, p. 7]. guo's own Linux runs used only 1–35 prompts each (Table 2, p. 8). Together these point to source/sink coverage as one plausible mechanism.
- [I] Cost contradiction with li2026llm. guo reports an average of $2.54 and 0.44 h per project, with a maximum of $18.15 and 10,661.98 s on icu (p. 7, Table 2 p. 8). li measures RepoAudit (Sonnet 3.5) at an average of $172.77 and a maximum of $1,247.66 per project, with a maximum runtime over 800 min [@li2026llm, p. 15, p. 16]. The projects and their sizes differ:
  - guo's projects average 251 KLoC, and its Linux modules cost $0.03–$0.86 (p. 7, p. 8).
  - li analyses modules of up to 3,924,621 LOC plus gpac and bitlbee, with no budget or timeout limits [@li2026llm, p. 6]. Which project cost the most in li is not reported in li's main text.
  - guo itself says cost depends on the number of source elements (p. 9).

  guo's per-project cost therefore should not be generalised to large repositories."""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
old2="| RQ3 | Average cost $2.54, 0.44 h and ~615K input tokens per project; $0.95 per true bug; o3-mini $0.30, DeepSeek R1 $0.57 | p. 7, p. 8, p. 16, p. 17 | V | moderate |"
new2=old2+"\n| RQ3 | Cost contradiction: li2026llm measures RepoAudit (Sonnet 3.5) at avg $172.77, max $1,247.66 and >800 min per project vs $2.54 / 0.44 h here; different projects and sizes (avg 251 KLoC here vs Linux modules up to 3.9M LOC, gpac, bitlbee in li) | p. 7, p. 8 | I | weak |\n| RQ2 | Tension with li2026llm (0/110 known C/C++ vulns, 92.77% SFDR): overlapping projects only in li's real-world set, at newer commits and partly different bug types; precision vs recall/SFDR; different labellers (see §9) | p. 7, p. 8 | I | weak |"
assert s.count(old2)==1
s=s.replace(old2,new2)
old3="Its strong self-reported precision vs li2026llm's independent replication is a key contradiction for RQ1/RQ2"
new3="Its strong self-reported precision and low cost vs li2026llm's independent evaluation (on different targets, commits and metrics; see §9) is a key tension for RQ1/RQ2/RQ3"
assert s.count(old3)==1
s=s.replace(old3,new3)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.content:
- [I] No deep-learning (fine-tuned) detectors are compared: informs LLM vs SAST, not LLM vs DL. Based on p. 4.
- [I] Backbones differ across tools (Claude Sonnet 4.6 vs GPT-5.4 vs GPT-4), so agent-vs-specialized comparisons mix workflow and model effects, partly controlled by the GPT-5.4 re-runs. Based on Table I (p. 4).
- [I] Documented tension with guo2025repoaudit (RepoAudit's own evaluation); both sides are confirmed in the texts and neither is a replication of the other. Based on the pages cited below.
  - Effectiveness. guo: RepoAudit (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) reproduces all 21 previously reported bugs and finds 19 new ones, 40 TPs / 11 FPs, precision 78.43%, on 15 C/C++ projects [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 7, p. 8]. li: RepoAudit (Sonnet 3.5) detects 0/110 and RepoAudit (GPT-5.4) 2/110 known C/C++ vulnerabilities (p. 7); real-world SFDR 92.77% as a 9-project average (p. 11).
  - Cost. guo: average $2.54 and 0.44 h per project, maximum $18.15 (icu) [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 7, p. 8]. li: average $172.77, maximum $1,247.66 per project, and over 800 min maximum runtime (p. 15, p. 16). Which project cost $1,247.66 is in Appendix C, which our PDF lacks.
  - Dataset. guo's targets are bug reports of prior tools [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 7]. li's controlled set is ReposVul CVEs from "the three repositories with the most cases" per CWE, and li does not name those repositories (p. 5). The targets overlap only with li's *real-world* set, where recall is not measured: linux/sound, linux/mm, linux/drivers/net, linux/drivers/peci and ImageMagick (Table III, p. 6; [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 7]). For 3 of these 5 the bug type differs: ImageMagick is NPD in guo but CWE-401 in li, linux/driver(s)/net is MLK vs CWE-416, and peci is UAF vs CWE-476. Sizes differ at every shared target. For example, linux/sound is 1,378,262 LoC in guo vs 1,253,234 in li, and guo analyses ImageMagick/MagickCore (242,555) while li analyses the whole ImageMagick repository (680,878). guo's "linux/driver/net" (914,025) is closer in size to li's linux/net (962,143) than to li's linux/drivers/net (3,924,621), so the module mapping is unclear. On li's linux/net, RepoAudit emits 3 warnings with an SFDR of 66.67% (Table VII, p. 11). On the other shared projects li's RepoAudit (Sonnet 3.5) emits 0 warnings (linux/sound, linux/mm, ImageMagick), 1 FP (linux/drivers/net) and 3 FPs (peci) (Table VII, p. 11).
  - Commit. guo analyses the versions used by the earlier works, and its new bugs are "in historic versions" [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 7, p. 8]. li uses current commits 6093a68 (Linux) and 3bf1076 (ImageMagick) (p. 6). guo's 4 Linux known bugs are all intra-procedural [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 8], and li notes that RepoAudit was evaluated on only 4 intra-function Linux cases (p. 7).
  - Metric. guo reports precision on the tool's own reports and reproduction of 21 known bugs. li reports recall on CVEs (controlled set) and SFDR (real-world set).
  - Labeller. guo does not describe how RepoAudit's own reports were judged TP/FP; only the Infer/CodeGuru reports are said to be labelled manually [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 14]. li used Codex labels with stratified manual validation (p. 11).
  - Scale. guo's projects average 251 KLoC, and its 4 Linux modules took only 1–35 prompts and $0.03–$0.86 each [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 7, p. 8]. li runs RepoAudit with no time or money budgets (p. 6) on modules up to 3,924,621 LOC; it emits 77 warnings on gpac and 374 on bitlbee (Tables III and VII, p. 6, p. 11). guo itself says cost depends on the number of source elements [@guo2025repoaudit, p. 9].
  - Explanation (ours). Target selection, code version, bug-type mapping, project scale and metric all differ, so the results are not directly comparable. RepoAudit made no LLM call on at least one project in li (0.00 tokens, Table XII, p. 16), and guo's Linux runs used very few prompts. Together with li's API-modelling analysis (p. 7), this points to source/sink coverage as one plausible mechanism for both the low recall and the cost spread.

## 10. Threats to validity
- Internal (confounds, leakage, selection): LLM self-labelling (see 9); pretraining contamination acknowledged (p. 18); single runs (p. 18); different backbones per tool (p. 4).
- External (generalisability of sample/context): C/C++ and Java only, 8 CWEs, 24 projects with several from one Linux commit (p. 18); tools limited to publicly available, runnable ones (p. 4).
- Construct (do metrics measure the concept?): SFDR measures false alarms among sampled warnings, not missed vulnerabilities; controlled precision is file-restricted (p. 6); all SAST severities counted equally (p. 7).
